summary.headline: Shivalik Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 33.4% YoY to ₹182.2 crore and PAT rose 44.9% to ₹33 crore, with FY27 revenue growth guided at 20-30%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 33.4% YoY to ₹182.2 crore, EBITDA rose 35.2% to ₹43.2 crore and PAT rose 44.9% to ₹33 crore. Shunts grew 18.7% while bimetals grew 7.4%, and management attributed roughly half of the revenue growth to higher silver prices. Management said margin gains came mainly from shunt conversion from strip to finished parts, which it considers sustainable. The company also received consent to operate for Phase 1 of its Pune facility for cell connecting systems and bus bar assemblies, serving one two-wheeler OEM for now.

financial_highlights.metric: Share of growth from value-add in shunts
financial_highlights.value: ~70-75% of shunt value-add growth from conversion to parts; rest from material/commodity

segments.name: Shunts
segments.commentary: Revenue up 18.7% YoY; strip sales to shunt customers down to about one-third of last year's level, with remaining strip being higher value-added. Management expects shunts at about 54-55% of standalone revenue.

segments.name: Bimetals (thermostatic)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 7.4% YoY; management says customers are signalling first quantity uptick in 4-5 quarters, mainly domestic. Expects about 44-45% of standalone revenue; utilisation about 40-45%.

segments.name: Contacts (wholly owned subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Expected to be 30-35% of consolidated revenue; about 60% of contacts revenue goes to switchgear. Silver price roughly doubled YoY, with about half of revenue growth attributed to silver.

segments.name: Cell connecting systems / bus bar and PCBA assemblies
segments.commentary: Minimal revenue in Q1 as full production began only in the last month of the quarter; expected 15-16% of total revenue in first year. Main Pune manufacturing becomes fully operational only in October.

guidance_outlook: FY27 overall revenue growth guided at roughly 20-30%, dependent on customer forecasts; management said it is early in the year.
Expects cell connecting systems and bus bar revenue to step up in the current and upcoming quarters, with Pune full operation from October.

Management sees a potential ₹300-400 crore business from the Pune facility in about 3 years, with about 10-15% in year 1, ₹150-200 crore in year 2 and ₹300 crore onwards thereafter; these figures are explicitly subject to change.
Pune incremental capex estimated at about ₹20-25 crore, with the high-capex processes already in place at Solon.
Expects one customer's share to stay below 17-18% in the maximum case, versus 35-40% at its historical peak.
capex_capacity: Pune Phase 1 received consent to operate after the quarter; currently capable of serving only one two-wheeler EV model.
Pune main manufacturing facility expected to be fully operational only in October 2026.
Welding capacity utilisation about 65-70%; can add shunt capacity within 2-3 months using spare ready-to-build capacity.
Thermostatic bimetal capacity utilisation about 40-45%; capacity expansion is slow and capex-intensive.
Pune incremental capex about ₹20-25 crore; the Pune facility has room for expansion.
demand_pricing: Large US customer has given expectations for this year that management describes as encouraging; the resurgence is in higher value-added business.
Two-wheeler EV and smart meter applications cited as main growth end-uses for shunts.
Shunt accuracy, not price, is the key buying criterion; a recently patented design by a large resistor customer is winning share, including from some Chinese OEMs.
Bimetal export opportunities with existing customers restarted after the US tariff pause; these are expected to add revenue in about 4 quarters.
Silver prices about double YoY and slightly lower QoQ; copper prices up substantially YoY.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 guidance for top line and margins, split by segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave overall revenue growth of about 20-30% and a segment mix: bimetal 44-45%, shunts 54-55% of standalone; contacts 30-35% and assemblies about 15-16% of consolidated revenue in year 1. No margin guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 33% growth is sustainable excluding commodity prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to a 20-30% range going forward and said about half of the revenue growth came from silver, with shunt value-add conversion driving margin gains that are considered sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Pune bus bar opportunity and incremental capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Potential business of ₹300-400 crore in about 3 years, with capex of about ₹20-25 crore since high-capex processes already exist at Solon; figures subject to change.

qa_highlights.question: Are new verticals or inorganic moves planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Two or three opportunities identified (greenfield or technology partnership) in electronics specialty material and automotive fuses; at least one or two may be announced soon, possibly via JV, licence or acquisition.

qa_highlights.question: How concentrated is the largest customer?
qa_highlights.answer: Peak exposure was 35-40%; even in the maximum case this year it will not exceed 17-18%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the bimetal business turning around?
qa_highlights.answer: For the first time in 4-5 quarters customers signal quantity uptick, mainly domestic, including real estate and infrastructure; export developments restarted, expected to add revenue in about 4 quarters.

risks_watch: Revenue growth is partly commodity-driven: silver roughly doubled YoY and copper rose substantially, and management says about half of growth came from silver.
Pune ramp depends on one OEM's EV two-wheeler model; the ₹300-400 crore opportunity is explicitly subject to change and phase 2 qualifications are still pending.
Bus bar and cell connecting system revenue is still minimal in Q1; watch October full operation and the next quarter's revenue step-up.
Bimetal volume recovery is early (quantities only, one quarter of evidence) and export developments are still in testing.
Management did not give margin guidance, and it cited employee cost increases alongside margin expansion.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the shunt and value-add story and on Pune's prospects, but evasive on specifics. Management declined to quantify several items under NDA (customer names, JV partners, the precious metal share) and repeatedly stressed that forecasts are early and subject to change.
key_quotes: Q1 FY27 is a strong start to the year and gives us further evidence that Shivalik is progressing higher on the value curve.
So, yes, that part is sustainable, because those parts are here to stay.

adds.what: Pune Phase 1 facility for cell connecting systems and bus bar assemblies (serves one two-wheeler OEM for now)

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at roughly 20-30%, dependent on customer forecasts; backing is partial, with Pune Phase 1 (consent received, full operation from October, ~₹20-25 cr incremental capex) and silver-driven pricing/mix, plus a one-customer order base, but no firm order book numbers.
